title: Minimum Time to Visit a Cell In a Grid
summary: Given a m x n grid with each cell containing a non-negative integer representing the minimum time required to visit that cell, you start at the top-left cell and must move to adjacent cells in one second per move.
statement: Given a m x n grid with each cell containing a non-negative integer representing the minimum time required to visit that cell, you start at the top-left cell and must move to adjacent cells in one second per move. The task is to find the minimum time needed to reach the bottom-right cell, or return -1 if it's unreachable.
constraints: Start at (0,0) at time zero and move one orthogonal cell every second; waiting in place is forbidden.
A cell may be entered only at a time at least its grid value.
Return the earliest bottom-right arrival, or -1 when the first move is impossible.
hints: If both starting neighbors require time beyond one, there is nowhere to move and the answer is -1.
Otherwise use Dijkstra because reaching a cell earlier never harms future options.
When a neighbor opens too late, oscillation adds time in steps of two; choose the first allowed time with the needed parity.
The adjusted edge arrival is the earliest feasible arrival from the current state, so Dijkstra finalizes the globally earliest destination time.

tests.explanation: Shortest-path search with parity-adjusted waits reaches the destination at time seven.
Neither neighbor can be entered at time one, so movement cannot begin.
